title: Fabrication Overview and the Role of Controlled Information
objective: Recognise fabrication as controlled work guided by drawings, specifications and authorised information.
safety_boundary: Conceptual fabrication overview only; no practical fabrication procedure is taught.

sections.heading: 1. Fabrication
sections.body: Fabrication turns specified materials into required components or structures through planned, controlled work.

sections.heading: 2. Job information
sections.body: Drawings, dimensions, specifications and procedures communicate the required result.

sections.heading: 3. Material identity
sections.body: Correct material identification matters because different materials have different properties and requirements.

sections.heading: 4. Verify before work
sections.body: Unclear or conflicting information must be resolved through an authorised person before practical work proceeds.
